title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

Continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming, with a rapid release cadence through late 2025: Sonnet 4.5 (Sept. 2025), Haiku 4.5 (Nov. 2025, matching or beating Sonnet 4 on several benchmarks at a fraction of the cost), and Opus 4.5 — Anthropic's smartest model of 2025, later described internally as the bar new releases had to clear.

---

## Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 (February 2026)

Anthropic kept up a breakneck pace into 2026: **Opus 4.6** shipped first, followed just 12 days later by **Sonnet 4.6** (Feb. 17, 2026). Sonnet 4.6 was a full upgrade across coding, computer use, long-horizon reasoning, agent planning, and design, with a **1M-token context window in beta**. In Claude Code, users preferred Sonnet 4.6 over Sonnet 4.5 about 70% of the time — and preferred it over Opus 4.5 (the November 2025 flagship) 59% of the time, continuing the pattern of each new Sonnet closing in on the prior Opus. Pricing held at $3/$15 per Mtok (input/output).

---

## Claude Opus 4.8 (May 2026)

Released May 28, 2026. Notable jumps: 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro (up from 64.3% for Opus 4.7), 88.6% on SWE-bench Verified, and a standout 96.7% on USAMO 2026 (vs. 69.3% for Opus 4.7) — the largest single-cycle math jump in the Opus line to date. Anthropic also reported the model is roughly 4x less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flawed code pass unremarked. It remains the strongest computer-use and browser-agent model Anthropic has tested, with a 1M-token context window (128K max output). Pricing unchanged at $5/$25 per Mtok; a Fast Mode variant runs ~2.5x faster at $10/$50 per Mtok.

---

## Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5: A New Model Class (June 2026)

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic introduced **Fable** and **Mythos** as a naming tier above Opus — "Mythos-class" models built for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. **Claude Fable 5** is the generally-available, safety-hardened release; **Claude Mythos 5** shares the same underlying capability but is offered only in limited release through *Project Glasswing* to approved customers. Both score 80.3% on SWE-bench Pro, well ahead of GPT-5.5's 58.6%, and Fable 5 was reported as the strongest model tested on frontier physics research while using roughly a third of the reasoning tokens of comparable models. Because Fable/Mythos-class capability in cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry is advanced enough to carry misuse risk, Anthropic ships them with safeguards that block or throttle output in those domains (Anthropic says over 95% of Fable sessions never trigger a fallback).

**Export-control episode:** in mid-June 2026, Anthropic briefly suspended all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 worldwide — including for foreign-national Anthropic employees — after a U.S. Department of Commerce directive citing unspecified national-security concerns about Fable 5. After an 18-day shutdown, Commerce lifted the requirement on June 30, 2026, once Anthropic agreed to proactively address model security risks, coordinate with the government on safety standards for future models, and report malicious activity. Global access was restored the same week.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)

Launched the same week Fable/Mythos access was restored, **Sonnet 5** is described by Anthropic as its most agentic Sonnet yet — able to plan, use browsers and terminals, and run autonomously at a level that previously required Opus-tier models. It scores 63.2% on an agentic-coding benchmark (vs. 58.1% for Sonnet 4.6 and 69.2% for Opus 4.8), closing much of the gap to Opus at a fraction of the cost. Sonnet 5 became the default model for Free and Pro users worldwide and in Claude Code, with a **native 1M-token context window**. Introductory pricing runs $2/$10 per Mtok through August 31, 2026, then reverts to $3/$15.

**Current model IDs (as of July 2026):**

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest tier |
| Sonnet 5 | `claude-sonnet-5` | Default free/Pro model; most agentic Sonnet yet |
| Opus 4.8 | `claude-opus-4-8` | Strongest computer-use/browser-agent model |
| Fable 5 | `claude-fable-5` | GA "Mythos-class" frontier model, safety-hardened |

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → 1M tokens (1M rolled out with Sonnet/Opus 4.6+ and is now native in Sonnet 5)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → four tiers with Fable/Mythos added above Opus in June 2026
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing — Sonnet 5 vs. Opus 4.8 is the starkest example yet
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon autonomy, and integration with external systems
- **Governance/safety:** As raw capability grows, so does external scrutiny — the June 2026 export-control episode over Fable 5/Mythos 5 was the first time a Claude model's availability was suspended by US government order
